domain_title: Accountability, evidence, risk decisions and lifecycle governance
title: Approval-as-end-state governance
canonical_definition: Governance effectively stops after initial approval while operation, change and retirement remain uncontrolled.

conditions: Deployment, Operation and Monitoring, Review and Evaluation, Retirement, and every material-change reassessment trigger.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Approval-as-end-state governance: Governance effectively stops after initial approval while operation, change and retirement remain uncontrolled.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show no post-deployment monitoring, model changes bypassing review, or retired systems retaining access?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Approval-as-end-state governance, or does it remain unknown?

antipattern_indicators: Retired systems retain access, data or contracts

conditions: Refer verified approval-as-end-state governance to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 1.5 (PDF p. 28), GOVERN 1.7 (PDF p. 28), MANAGE 4.1 (PDF p. 38), MANAGE 4.3 (PDF p. 38)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on maintaining monitoring and periodic review, responding to incidents and planning decommissioning. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where initial approval is treated as sufficient for operation, changes and shutdown. The mechanism can have an operational effect where material changes bypass review, incidents go unhandled, or retired integrations retain access or data without authorization.
potential_consequences: Behavior, risk or access can drift beyond approved conditions after initial release.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether initial approval is treated as sufficient for operation, changes and shutdown. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether material changes bypass review, incidents go unhandled, or retired integrations retain access or data without authorization. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review trace representative monitoring alerts, release changes and a retirement or exit exercise to final disposition. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether initial approval is treated as sufficient for operation, changes and shutdown. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether material changes bypass review, incidents go unhandled, or retired integrations retain access or data without authorization. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide trace representative monitoring alerts, release changes and a retirement or exit exercise to final disposition. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: Trace representative monitoring alerts, release changes and a retirement or exit exercise to final disposition.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether initial approval is treated as sufficient for operation, changes and shutdown, and separately check whether material changes bypass review, incidents go unhandled, or retired integrations retain access or data without authorization. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use trace representative monitoring alerts, release changes and a retirement or exit exercise to final disposition. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: An explicitly limited operating approval can be valid when monitoring, review and expiry remain active.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in F5 alone cannot establish AP-F5 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows approval-as-end-state governance
Implementation or operating evidence shows approval-as-end-state governance
Presence or tested absence of approval-as-end-state governance is unresolved within scope
